request.recipient: Input Output Global / IO: Hydra, with Intersect providing administrative treasury governance
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund IO: Hydra workstreams for performance optimization, operational excellence, ecosystem support, and developer experience toward a feature-complete and hardened Hydra v2.

claims.claim: Hydra is described as the only production-grade Layer 2 on Cardano and a state-channel scaling solution with sub-second finality, near-zero fees, high throughput, and Cardano L1 settlement as the backstop.
The proposal says Hydra is already used or demonstrated by Delta DeFi, Masumi, Hydra Doom, Glacier Drop, Intersect voting infrastructure, VTech Labs, Blockfrost, and Midgard.

The proposal claims Cardano L1 has over two hours of finality, about $0.17 payment fees, $1 to $3 DeFi transaction fees, and roughly 7 to 10 TPS, making high-performance applications uncompetitive on L1.
The proposal claims competing ecosystems offer 400ms to 2s finality, sub-cent fees, and 1,000 to 7,000+ TPS, causing builders to exclude Cardano before evaluating its strengths.
The proposal claims the funded work will improve Hydra snapshot signing and memory profile by 2x to 10x and reduce L1 fees through on-chain contract optimization.
The proposal claims Hydra applications can increase Cardano ecosystem activity, TVL, monthly active users, transactions, throughput capacity, reliability, uptime, and annual protocol revenue.
The proposal claims Hydra head lifecycle transactions and optionally routed internal head fees can create usage-linked L1 fee accrual that scales with adoption.
The proposal states the requested treasury amount is ₳5,100,781 and that funding will be milestone-gated with independent third-party assurance and Intersect administrative treasury governance.
The proposal identifies provisional users under evaluation including Bodega Market, Atlas Defi, Wingriders, Houselink, European Public Network, and others.
The proposal asserts that if Hydra improvements slip, existing use cases risk migrating to competing chains and attracting new builders to Cardano will be hard.

summary: The document requests ₳5,100,781 for Hydra v2 hardening across performance, operations, ecosystem support, and developer experience, but most high-materiality adoption, economic, and technical benefit claims are asserted without detailed budget, feasibility, alternatives, failure-mode, or community-impact analysis in the supplied text.
